page: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 640 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% results in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as in Passmark CPU tests covering extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with large-block read and write speeds reaching top 10% tiers. In real-world application benchmarks, the server demonstrates strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Redis SET operations, while maintaining average performance in single-threaded compression, static web serving, and database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory bandwidth provide reliable, non-burstable compute resources suitable for production workloads. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this server highly effective for general-purpose enterprise applications, software development pipelines, Redis caching layers, and moderate-scale multi-threaded data processing. It is also capable of handling medium-sized language model inference, showing strong text generation speeds for 7B parameter models.
